mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -39.6% (t-1w) to -24.4% (t-0w), a 15.2 percentage-point weekly gain. This sustained workplace return signals normalization of commuting patterns, which directly drives weekday retail foot traffic and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 15.2 points week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES declines below -30% in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has stabilized near -46.7% (t-0w) after volatile swings. When transit remains depressed below -45% for two consecutive weeks, consumers substitute toward personal-vehicle retail trips and outdoor recreation, increasing RETAIL_REC in the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -45% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w is -46.7%, t-1w is -54.3%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 14 days, or TRANSIT recovers above -40% within one week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility swung from +18.1% (t-2w) to -13.9% (t-0w), a 32-point collapse. This sharp outdoor-activity contraction signals weather deterioration or policy tightening that simultaneously suppresses RETAIL_REC. The mechanism operates over one week with immediate effect.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 32 points from t-2w to t-0w
regime_hint: tightening restrictions or adverse seasonal shift
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a >20-point PARKS decline, or PARKS recovers above +5% within one week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC move inversely when essential-goods demand is high and discretionary spending is suppressed. At t-0w, GROCERY_PHARM is -4.7% (near baseline) while RETAIL_REC is -43.7% (deeply depressed). This divergence indicates consumers are prioritizing essentials; if GROCERY_PHARM remains stable and RETAIL_REC gap narrows, retail recovery follows within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within -10% to 0% while RETAIL_REC gap to GROCERY_PHARM narrows
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at t-0w is -4.7%, RETAIL_REC is -43.7%
regime_hint: demand reallocation from discretionary to essential
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines below -15% or RETAIL_REC remains more than 40 points below GROCERY_PHARM in the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stabilized at 12.4% (t-0w) after hovering around 14-15% in prior weeks. Stabilization of home-confinement levels signals policy regime shift toward steady-state restrictions rather than tightening. Under steady-state regime, RETAIL_REC recovers modestly as consumers adapt and plan discretionary trips within permitted bounds.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL variance falls below 2 percentage points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at t-0w is 12.4%, t-1w is 15.3%, t-2w is 14.0%
regime_hint: steady state with stable confinement levels
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above 16% or falls below 10% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility collapsed 32 points from t-2w to t-0w, indicating seasonal weather deterioration or policy closure of outdoor spaces. This environmental shock simultaneously depresses RETAIL_REC because outdoor retail (markets, terraces) and recreation are complementary activities. The effect is immediate and persists for one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines below 0% after being positive
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week after PARKS turns negative, or PARKS recovers above +10% within one week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are jointly depressed at t-0w (-24.4% and -46.7% respectively). When both remain below -20% and -45% respectively for two weeks, the combined effect of low commuting and low transit use suppresses retail foot traffic. Recovery requires both series to improve simultaneously; if only one improves, RETAIL_REC remains constrained.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -20% AND TRANSIT below -45% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at t-0w is -24.4%, TRANSIT is -46.7%
regime_hint: restricted mobility regime with low workplace and transit access
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises more than 5 percentage points over the next two weeks, or either WORKPLACES exceeds -15% or TRANSIT exceeds -40% within one week.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown high volatility (range: -53.4% to -43.7% over four weeks) with no clear trend direction. This volatility indicates unstable consumer confidence and policy uncertainty. When volatility persists (standard deviation of weekly changes > 5 points), RETAIL_REC remains suppressed over the next four weeks as consumers delay discretionary spending.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week changes exceed ±5 percentage points in two of the last three weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC ranged from -53.4% to -43.7% with swings of 5-10 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes within a 3-point band for two consecutive weeks, or rises above -35% in the next four weeks.
